# The Liṅga He Could Not Uproot

## He Cannot Pull Up a Liṅga Made of Sand

Hanuman carries mountains. He crosses an ocean in a leap. He is, across four groups of this volume, the figure whose only real constraint is that Rāma has not asked him to do the larger thing.[^2]

**In *Brahma Vaivarta Purāṇa*, Brahma-khaṇḍa 46, he tries to lift a liṅga that Sītā has just made out of sand, and he cannot.**

**And then he collapses unconscious.**[^1]

⚑ **This is the only outright failure of strength anywhere in this build.** Not a restraint, not a deferral, not a capacity throttled by somebody else's judgement — **an attempt that does not work, in public, followed by a physical collapse.**

**And it has a chapter locator**, which almost nothing about his limits does.

## The Delay Is His

The setup matters, because the failure is downstream of something the volume never dwells on.

**He is sent to Kailāsa to fetch a liṅga**, so that Rāma can consecrate a shrine **in atonement for killing Rāvaṇa.**[^1]

**He is delayed.**[^1]

⚑ **The essay says nothing about why**, and that silence is worth marking. **A figure whose distinguishing capacity is speed — whose epithets are welded to it, whose *gati* outruns every creature's — misses a deadline.**[^3]

**Sītā, to avoid losing the auspicious hour, fashions a liṅga from sand and the consecration proceeds.**[^1]

⚠ **So the shrine that exists at Rāmeśvaram exists because Hanuman was late.** ⚑ **And the whole of what follows — the attempt, the failure, the collapse — happens to a man arriving with a genuine article that is no longer needed.**

## The Motive Is Protectiveness

What he does next is the part that has been misread as pride, and the essay supplies the motive plainly.

**Returning with the Kailāsa liṅga, he finds it superseded, and he is distressed at what he perceived as *"Śiva's own dishonour."***[^1]

⚑ **That is not wounded standing. It is an objection on somebody else's behalf.** **The complaint is that a god has been given sand when stone from his own mountain was on its way**, and Hanuman is the one who was carrying it.

⚠ **And this build has met that structure before, aimed at a different god.** ⚑ **Premnidhi's worship manuals describe Hanuman as permanently watchful, with a *jealous protectiveness over how Rāma's attention gets spent*, and wounded feelings when devotees bypass him.**[^4] **Here the same protectiveness is pointed at Śiva's honour rather than Rāma's attention, and it produces an *action* rather than a feeling.**

⚑ **Which makes this the clearest instance in the build of that disposition doing damage.** ⚠ **The routing material shows the protectiveness as an arrangement; here it is a man trying to destroy a consecrated object because he thinks the arrangement is beneath its beneficiary** — and being unable to.

## Analytical Case Study: The Only Limit Nobody Chose

Set this beside every other limit in the corpus and it is the odd one out.

**`restraint-was-rama-managing-him` records the pattern**: Rāma privately certain that Hanuman *could* stop the sun and grind Death's noose, and quietly declining to commission it — so that the celebrated humility is **an administrative outcome** rather than a real ceiling.[^2] ⚑ **Every limit in that account is somebody's decision.**

**The volume's other limits are the same shape.** ⚠ The envoy's brief. The vow not to initiate war. The refusal of Mainaka's rest. **Each is a constraint accepted, and each is therefore evidence of discipline rather than of capacity.**

⚑ **This one is not accepted.** **He tries, at full effort, on his own initiative, and the thing does not move.**

⚠ **And that is why it cannot be converted.** **A declined feat proves restraint; a failed feat proves nothing except that the feat was beyond him** — and the volume has no apparatus for that, because its entire treatment of his powers is organised around the question of *whether they were used*, never around whether they sufficed.

⚑ **Which suggests the reason nobody in thirty-seven devotional essays mentions this episode.** **It is not embarrassing in the way a lapse is.** **It is *unusable*** — there is no reading on which it demonstrates a virtue, and the survey register that reports it is the only one with no thesis for it to damage.

## Revived by His Own Praises

The recovery is as strange as the failure and the essay gives it in five words.

**He collapses, and is revived by his praises being recited.**[^1]

⚑ **The remedy for the collapse is being told about himself.**

⚠ **Which is the third instance of that mechanism in this group alone.** **Jāmbavān recites his deeds at the ocean and his capability returns. Jāmbavān names him a Rudra incarnation in the *Nāṭaka* and his restraint departs. And here his praises are recited over an unconscious body and he wakes.**[^5]

⚑ **The tradition is consistent about the mechanism and unbothered by its range.** **Reciting what Hanuman is does something to Hanuman, reliably, in three different registers with three different outcomes** — and no contributor anywhere assembles the three.

⚠ **And note what is *not* the remedy.** **Rāma does not console him. Sītā does not apologise. Nobody explains that the sand liṅga was an emergency measure.** ⚑ **The correction applied to a man who has just discovered a limit is a recitation of his greatness** — which is precisely the register this build has recorded as removing calibration rather than restoring it.[^5]

## Sītā Improvised and It Held

The other half of the episode is a small masterpiece and the volume passes over it entirely.

⚑ **Faced with a fixed deadline and a missing component, Sītā substitutes the material to hand and the rite works.** **The sand liṅga is consecrated. It stays consecrated. It cannot be removed, by the strongest being in the story, at full effort.**

⚠ **The material was never the point.** **The auspicious hour was**, and she optimised for the constraint that could not be relaxed rather than for the one that could.

⚑ **And the tradition ratifies her judgement in the strongest available way**: not by praising it, but by **making her improvisation immovable.** **The sand holds and the Kailāsa stone has to be installed somewhere else** — as **Hanumal-liṅga, north of Rāmeśvaram**, a second shrine for a component that arrived late.[^1]

⚠ **This build has recorded the volume's habit of printing its best material as scaffolding.**[^6] ⚑ **This is the sharpest instance yet.** **A story about substituting under a hard deadline, and about the substitute proving more durable than the authentic article, sits inside an essay surveying liṅga-origins — and the essay's interest is in why there are two shrines.**

## What the Volume Does With It

Almost nothing, and the distribution is by now familiar.

⚑ **The episode appears in one survey essay, in the comparative group, with a locator.**[^1] ⚠ **It does not appear in the thirty-seven *Character & Virtue* and *Devotion to Rāma* essays this build has read** — though those were not read looking for it, and the absence is *not found in the range read* rather than an absence.

**And the survey essay's own framing is about the shrines.** ⚑ **The failure, the collapse, the distress and the improvisation are all reported as the explanation for a geographical fact**: why the Rāmeśvaram liṅga is one thing and Hanumal-liṅga another.

⚠ **Which is the levelling this build has now recorded twice in this one essay.** ⚑ **The same plurality machinery that lets the volume hold three birth accounts without collapsing lets it hold a mortal sin and a public failure at the same weight as a place-name.**[^7] **Nothing is foregrounded because nothing is ranked**, and a reader learns what the tradition considers serious from somewhere else or not at all.

### Source-Update: The Injury, and the Remedy the Other Section Records

⛑⛑ **Added 2026-08-18. The volume holds this episode twice, in two sections that do not cite each other — and each keeps a half the other drops.**

⭐ **The *Carit*'s narrative gives the cause and the injury in full.** Rāma, troubled at having killed a Brahmin — Rāvaṇa by birth — **resolves on Agastya's advice to install a liṅga and sends Hanumān to Kailāsa.** ⚑ **He is delayed *seeking Śiva's darśana through prolonged austerity*** — **not by distance, and not by any obstacle: by devotion of his own.** The auspicious hour runs out; **Sītā shapes a small liṅga from sand as a diversion**, and Rāma installs it on the sages' advice. It becomes **Rāmanāthaliṅgam.**[^8]

⭐⭐ **Then the part the narrative does not soften**: he returns, distressed, and **tries to uproot the sand-liṅga with his own tail — succeeding only in exhausting himself, losing his grip, and falling unconscious. Sītā revives him.**[^8]

⚠ **The *Carit* records the injury and stops there.** ⭐ **The south-India temple survey records the settlement**: the liṅga Sītā made **can never be moved**, and Hanumān's from Kailāsa **is installed right beside it** — with the rule attached that ***"anyone visiting Rāmeśvaram without also seeing Hanumān's liṅga would not receive the full merit of the pilgrimage."***[^9]

⚑⚑ **Both halves on the page now, because neither section is complete alone.** ⭐ **The narrative supplies the *cause* of the failure — his own austerity — which is the detail that makes the episode about devotion competing with duty rather than about slowness.** **The survey supplies the *remedy*, and the remedy is not consolation: it makes the second liṅga a condition on the first's merit.**

⚠ **A tension the two sections leave standing.** **On the narrative's telling he is revived by the person whose object he was trying to destroy.** ⭐ **Neither text remarks on it, and the survey's settlement quietly reverses the outcome he was reaching for by other means** — he does not move her liṅga, and the pilgrimage is made incomplete without his.

## Implementation Workflow

**When you arrive late with the right thing and find a substitute already in place, the decision is not about quality.** ⚑ **The substitute has a property yours does not: it is installed.** **Arguing that yours is better is arguing about the wrong variable**, and this build's episode ends with the late arrival unconscious on the floor.

**Check whether you are defending a standard or defending your journey.** ⚠ **The stated motive here is a god's dishonour, and it may be entirely sincere.** ⚑ **It is also, structurally, the objection of somebody who has carried a mountain-stone a very long way for nothing** — and the two are indistinguishable from inside. **The test is whether you would still object if somebody else had fetched it.**

⚑ **And when a deadline is genuinely fixed, optimise for the constraint that cannot move.** ⚠ **Sītā's sand liṅga is not a compromise; it is a correct reading of which requirement was hard.** **The auspicious hour could not be rescheduled and the material could be changed, and she changed the changeable one.** **Most missed deadlines are cases where the reverse assumption went unexamined.**

## Evidence, Tensions, Open Questions

One *Aṅka* essay for the whole episode,[^1] and five of this build's pages for the comparisons.[^2][^3][^4][^5][^6][^7]

**Bounded.** 🚩 **SINGLE SOURCE.** ⚑ **The episode is reported by one contributor with a chapter locator — *Brahma Vaivarta Purāṇa*, Brahma-khaṇḍa 46 — and this build has not checked it.** `[TRADITION-CLAIM — verified]` as the essay's citation; **not verified against the Purāṇa.**

**Bounded again, and severely.** ⚠ **The essay supplies no dialogue, and names no other party's actions during the collapse.** ⚑ **Who recited the praises is not stated.** **Nothing here claims to know who was present or what was said.**

⚠ **And the reason for the delay is not given.** ⚑ **This page's observation that a figure defined by speed missed a deadline is a claim about the reported facts, not about a cause the essay supplies.**

🔴 **A tension preserved.** **A failure of strength with a locator, against a volume whose treatment of his powers assumes sufficiency throughout and whose only recorded limits are constraints somebody chose.** **No contributor puts the two together.**

**Open question.** ⚑ **Does any devotional essay in the volume mention Hanumal-liṅga?** **Two shrines at Rāmeśvaram is a checkable fact about a major pilgrimage site**, and whether the *Devotees, Legends & Worship* group — twenty-five essays, unread — carries the episode without the failure would establish whether the volume has one story here or two.

## Author Tensions & Convergences

The essay reporting this is the same one that reports the Brahmin-killing, and the two items share a property worth naming.

⚑ **Both are *etiological*.** **They explain why a shrine is where it is.** ⚠ **And that is the register in which a tradition can afford to say almost anything about a figure**, because the story is not being told about him — it is being told about a place, and he is in it.

**Which is a mechanism this build should hold onto.** ⚑ **Material that would be unprintable as biography is routinely printable as topography.** **A devotional essay cannot say Hanuman failed; a shrine-origin story can, because the point of the story is the shrine.**

⚠ **And it predicts where else to look.** ⚑ **The volume's hardest material about Hanuman is likely to sit wherever the essays are explaining something other than Hanuman** — the Purāṇic survey, the comparative section, the regional literatures — **and this build has now found the third lapse, a mortal sin, a public failure and a full-scale boast in exactly those places.**

**Upādhyāy is not braver than the devotional contributors.** ⚑ **He is writing about liṅgas.**

## Cross-Domain Handshakes

**[[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/sunk-cost-fallacy|Sunk Cost Fallacy]].** That page's mechanism is that **past spending is gone and should be irrelevant to what you do next, and the brain refuses** — the $15 ticket that keeps you in a film you hate, the annual fee that makes every subsequent service feel free, **the compulsion to throw good after bad because bad has already gone.** ⚑ **Hanuman has just carried a stone from Kailāsa, and the stone is now worthless.**

**What the pairing produces is a form of the fallacy the page does not treat: sunk cost expressed as *destruction* rather than as persistence.** ⚠ **The film-goer stays in his seat — the wasted action is passive.** ⚑ **Hanuman attacks the substitute.** **When the thing that made your investment worthless is an object in front of you, the fallacy stops being *continue* and becomes *remove the alternative***, which is a much more damaging shape and arrives with a moral justification attached.

⚑ **And the justification is the tell.** ⚠ **Nobody says *I stayed because I paid*; they say the film improved.** **Nobody says *I carried this a long way for nothing*; they say a god has been dishonoured.** **The rationalisation is always about the thing rather than about the expenditure**, and this build cannot separate them here and does not need to: **the behaviour is identical either way, and the diagnostic is whether you would object if somebody else had done the carrying.**

**[[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/timing-patience-strategic-delay|Timing, Patience, and Strategic Delay]].** That page holds that **the right move at the wrong time fails**, that timing is often more important than the move, and that **impatience is the mark of the weak while patience is the mark of the strong** — delay as the strategist's instrument. ⚑ **This episode is the inverse case, and the corpus's own four-axis framework makes it sharper.**

⚠ **This build has recorded *timing* as the fourth axis of the volume's best structure** — intelligence to act, discernment to judge, strength to carry through, **and timing to know when to move** — drawn from Rāma's own instructions.[^6] ⚑ **Here the figure that framework is built on is the one who is late**, and the entire episode is the consequence.

⚑ **What the pairing yields is that the strategic literature treats delay as *chosen* and has almost nothing to say about deadlines that are exogenous.** ⚠ **An auspicious hour cannot be waited out.** **Where the optimal moment is set by something other than your judgement, patience is not an instrument — it is the failure mode** — and the whole vocabulary of strategic delay inverts. ⚑ **Sītā, who has no strategic reputation in this literature at all, is the one who reads the constraint correctly**, and she does it by giving up on the material rather than on the hour.

## The Live Edge

The unresolved thing is whether this is a story about Hanuman at all.

⚑ **Read one way it is a genuine limit**: the strongest figure in the epic meets something he cannot move, and the something is a consecrated object, which would make the point theological rather than physical — **consecration binds in a way strength does not reach.** ⚠ **The essay does not say that, and the reading is available and unstated.**

**Read the other way it is a story about Sītā**, and Hanuman is the foil. ⚑ **The narrative work is all hers**: she identifies the binding constraint, improvises, and produces something that survives an assault by the story's strongest being. **His failure is what demonstrates her success.**

⚠ **And the second reading explains a detail the first does not.** ⚑ **Why is the sand liṅga immovable?** **Not because sand is strong — because it was consecrated at the right hour.** **The episode's whole physics is that timing beats material**, which is a claim about her decision and not about his strength.

**This build cannot settle which the Purāṇa intends**, and the essay is not asking. ⚑ **What can be said is that the volume filed it under Hanuman and the story's centre of gravity is somewhere else** — which is the third time in this group a contributor has reported material whose best subject he is not writing about.

## Connected Concepts

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/restraint-was-rama-managing-him|Restraint Was Rāma Managing Him]] — every other limit in the corpus, all of them chosen by somebody
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/a-sin-an-expiation-a-shrine|A Sin, an Expiation, a Shrine]] — the atonement this errand was for, from the same essay
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/a-jealous-kind-of-grace|A Jealous Kind of Grace]] — the same protectiveness, aimed at Rāma's attention rather than Śiva's honour
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/being-told-what-you-are|Being Told What You Are]] — reciting his greatness as an operation, here performed on an unconscious body
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/speed-bound-to-restraint|Speed Bound to Restraint]] — the epithets welded to speed, and the deadline they did not meet
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/hubs/hanumanic-strategy-hub|Hanumanic Strategy Hub]] — the build this page belongs to

Baldev Upādhyāy, M.A., D.Litt., Sāhityācārya**, pp. 93–95 (mid), in the ***Across Literature & Tradition*** group. For ***Brahma Vaivarta Purāṇa*, Brahma-khaṇḍa 46**: Hanuman **sent to fetch a Kailāsa liṅga to atone for killing Rāvaṇa**; **delayed**; **Sītā fashioning a sand-liṅga to avoid missing the auspicious consecration hour**; his distress on returning at what he perceived as ***"Śiva's own dishonour"***; his attempt to uproot her liṅga; his **failure and collapse into unconsciousness**, **revived by his praises being recited**; and **Rāma installing the Kailāsa liṅga separately as Hanumal-liṅga, north of Rāmeśvaram.** ⚠ **No dialogue is given, no other party's actions during the collapse are specified, and no reason is given for the delay.** ⚠ The essay hedges the frame: the story *"is said to have"* been given by Rāma. 🚩 SINGLE SOURCE. `[TRADITION-CLAIM — verified]` as the essay's citation; **not checked against the Purāṇa.**

# The Occipital Etiology of Visions and Voices

## A Voice, and Whose Voice It Is

The most consequential events in the history of religion are, very often, a person hearing something.

Bodri gives them a location:

> Sometimes people won't just see lights but will even see visions or special forms in the light, or even hear voices when they meditate. These instances are usually caused by the **chi entering the tiny nadi in the vicinity of the ear**, or **trying to penetrate through the occipital region of the brain**.[^1]

Two sites. One for what you hear, one for what you see. Both in the head, both physiological, both — on this account — the ordinary consequence of a practice working on the body.

That is the deflation, and it is not the interesting part of the page. The interesting part is what he says next about **which** voice you hear.

## The Sequence, In Order

Before the content question, the phenomenology — because Nan gives it as an ordered sequence rather than a list, and the order is the part a practitioner can actually check against.

**It begins with darkness.** *One may notice darkness in front of the eyes when half asleep.*[^3] Not light. The visual field goes dark first, in a state between waking and sleeping.

**Then a dreamlike state**, and gradually images appear — accompanied, he notes, by affect: *feelings of love and joy or sadness and dread*.[^3]

**Then, if the practitioner does not get caught, a change.** *Knowing that light follows the darkness. After passing through this stage one feels somewhat more awake.*[^3]

**And then the lights.** *Points of light, like a fluorescent star, may appear in front of your eyes, sparkling in different shapes and colors* — which he says are connected with physiology.[^3]

The auditory sequence runs in parallel and is more specific:

> When ch'i reaches the back of the head, a person might hear **wonderful inner sounds or experience ringing or pressure in his ears**. This phenomenon is produced by ch'i working to open the ch'i route in the brain. **The vibration or trembling of ch'i causes some brain wave activity.** If one's intelligence is not clear and bright enough, then illusions deep inside the subconscious will result.[^3]

Two things about this ordering are worth holding.

**The unglamorous symptoms come first and are the reliable ones.** Darkness, ringing, pressure — these are dull, common, and easy to dismiss as fatigue. On this account they are the earliest and most trustworthy indication that anything is happening at all, and they precede everything a practitioner would want to report.

**And the sequence has a fork in it.** *If one's intelligence is not clear and bright enough* the subconscious material takes over; if it is, the stage is passed and the practitioner comes out more awake. **The same physiological event produces either a passage or a delusion**, and what decides it is not further practice but the condition of the person when it arrives.

## The Content Comes From You

The mechanism only produces an event. Something else produces its contents, and the source is named:

> **One who has deep religious beliefs may have illusions of hearing the voice of God or Buddha.** Often the voice will speak of the past or future.[^2]

*God or Buddha* — and which one you get is not determined by the chi. It is determined by what you already hold.

Set out what that claims. The same physiological event, at the same site, in two practitioners of different traditions, produces two different divine speakers. The mechanism is invariant; the identity of the visitor is supplied by the recipient.

Which makes the content **diagnostic of the practitioner and evidentially worthless about the source.** A Christian contemplative hearing Christ and a Buddhist hearing the Buddha are not two data points about who is really speaking. They are two data points about who was sitting.

Nan's fuller description makes the mechanics of the supply explicit: as chi affects the nerves at the back of the head, a dreamlike state develops and images appear, and *many people have dream images accompanied by feelings of love and joy or sadness and dread*. Then the key clause — **these images and feelings match subconscious functions which give rise to one's mental states, thoughts and concepts.**[^3]

The images match what is already in the person. The physiology opens a channel; the person fills it.

## Keating, From Inside Christianity

The most valuable thing on this page is that Bodri does not leave the argument inside his own tradition. He quotes Thomas Keating — a Trappist monk, one of the architects of centering prayer, writing as a Christian contemplative to Christian contemplatives:

> **External visions and voices can be misunderstood. Even saints have misunderstood what God has said to them.** Divine communications of an intelligible kind have to be **filtered through the human psyche and one's cultural conditioning**. … Since one can never tell which percentage group a particular communication belongs to, if one follows these communications without discretion, one can get into all kinds of trouble. **There is no guarantee that any particular communication to an individual is actually coming from God.**[^4]

Every element of the Chan analysis is here, in the vocabulary of a completely different tradition and without any of the physiology.

**The content is filtered through the psyche and cultural conditioning** — which is Nan's *images match subconscious functions*, said theologically.

**Even saints have misunderstood** — the failure is not confined to the unprepared, which is the same finding as the Hakuin material elsewhere in this build.

**And no guarantee**, in a text written by someone who believes such communications sometimes genuinely occur. That is the crucial feature. Keating is not a sceptic. He grants the possibility of divine communication in full and still says the recipient cannot tell.

## Implementation Workflow

If it happens — a voice, a figure, a communication with content — the useful sequence has three steps and none of them is deciding whether it was real.

**First, note the physical.** Was there pressure at the back of the head, ringing or fullness in the ears, the half-asleep darkness before images appeared? Those are the reported precursors, and their presence is information you can gather in the moment and will not remember accurately later.

**Second, ask whose voice.** Not *was it God* — **was it a figure from the tradition you already hold?** If a lifelong Catholic hears Christ and a lifelong Buddhist hears the Buddha, the identity is not evidence, and you can establish this about your own case without adjudicating anything metaphysical.

**Third, and this is Keating's contribution, treat the content as advice rather than authority.** *If one follows these communications without discretion, one can get into all kinds of trouble.* Whatever the source, the message arrived through your psyche and your conditioning, and is therefore exactly as reliable as any other product of those.

The practical form of that: if the communication tells you something you already wanted to hear, or something that flatters, or something that would be very difficult to check — those are the conditions in which the filtering has most likely done the work.

And the thing not to do, which the material is emphatic about: do not chase it, and do not build a practice around producing more.

## Analytical Case Study: Two Traditions, One Conclusion, Two Kinds of Evidence

The convergence between the Chan physiology and the Trappist theology is the strongest thing on this page, and it is worth being precise about what it does and does not establish.

**What it establishes.** Two contemplative traditions with no shared vocabulary, no shared cosmology and no shared account of what a vision *is* both concluded that the content of visions and voices cannot be trusted as evidence about their source. One reached it by tracking chi to the back of the head; the other by reflecting on the epistemology of divine communication. **Independent routes to one conclusion is the strongest kind of corroboration available in a field with no experiments.**

**What it does not establish.** The two are not saying the same thing about *what is happening*. Keating holds that some communications are genuinely from God and the recipient cannot identify which. Nan and Bodri hold that the event is chi in the occipital region and the contents are subconscious material. Those are different claims. **The agreement is entirely on the epistemic verdict and not at all on the ontology**, and Bodri quotes Keating as though the agreement went further than it does.

That is a real instance of this book's characteristic move — the practice survives translation, the mystique does not — and here it costs something. Keating's caution is *inside* a framework where the visions might be divine; extracted into Bodri's, it becomes support for a claim Keating does not make.

**And a third thing the convergence establishes that neither author states.** If both traditions independently developed a warning literature about this, then both traditions had a problem with it. **The existence of the caution is evidence about the base rate**, in Christian contemplative practice as much as in Chan — which means visionary experience under sustained contemplative discipline is common enough, in both, to have required a standing correction.

## Māra, and What the State Depends On

Nan's account names the danger and then makes it conditional in an unusually specific way:

> **States of Mara, or demonic delusion, may occur at this stage.** These states depend upon one's **wisdom, thought, personality, psychological propensities, and physiological condition**. They are very complicated. Without the guidance of a very perceptive master, and in the absence of self-confidence, healthy intelligence, and correct thinking, **a person may be led down the wrong road**.[^3]

Five dependencies, and only one of them is spiritual.

*Wisdom* is the tradition's own variable. *Thought*, *personality* and *psychological propensities* are dispositional — what kind of person you are, independent of practice. *Physiological condition* is the body.

So the outcome of this stage is being predicted from a profile that is mostly **not about how well you have practised.** Two practitioners with identical discipline and different temperaments should, on this account, get different results — and the one with the more fragile constitution gets the worse one.

That is an unusually honest thing for a practice manual to say, and it converges with the dream-yoga screening criteria elsewhere in this build: certain people should not do certain practices, and the exclusion is about disposition rather than merit.

The protective factors listed are equally unmystical: **a very perceptive master, self-confidence, healthy intelligence, correct thinking.**[^3] Three of the four are ordinary psychological robustness. Which is a considerably more sober account of who gets into trouble than *insufficient devotion*.

## The Zen Answer

Against all of this, the recommended response is remarkably plain:

> The Zen school, commenting on this type of experience, says simply **to ignore it all because it is all mara, or illusion**. Furthermore, it's only by ignoring it through detachment that you can pass through it to higher spiritual states of knowing, for **the rule of cultivation is the emptiness of detachment all the way**.[^1]

Not interpret it. Not test it. Not seek a teacher to adjudicate it. **Ignore it.**

And the reason given is not that the phenomena are unimportant but that ignoring is the *only route through* — the material is a stage, and detachment is how you pass a stage rather than how you avoid one.

Nan's version adds a detail that makes the instruction less bleak: *when a person understands this, he can ignore phenomena of this sort, **knowing that light follows the darkness**. After passing through this stage one feels somewhat more awake.*[^3]

So there is an after. The half-asleep darkness, the images, the voices — these are described as a passage with something on the far side of it, and the ignoring is what gets you there.

Which is the same structure as the crescendo instruction elsewhere in this cluster: the phenomena proliferate, you do not manage them, and they resolve. **The tradition's advice about visions is procedurally identical to its advice about bodily sensations**, and neither passage notices the other.

## Evidence, Tensions, Open Questions

**Strongest support.** The convergence with Keating, arrived at independently from an entirely different tradition and epistemology.[^4] And the content-supply claim — *one who has deep religious beliefs may have illusions of hearing the voice of God or Buddha* — is checkable in principle against the distribution of visionary content across traditions.[^2]

**The tension the source does not close.** Keating grants that some communications are genuinely divine and says the recipient cannot tell which; Bodri quotes him in support of an account where the event is chi and the content is subconscious material. **The agreement is epistemic and the ontologies are incompatible**, and the quotation is deployed as though it were not.

**A second tension.** The Zen instruction is to ignore it all as māra; Nan's account says the outcome depends on five dispositional and physiological factors and warns that *without the guidance of a very perceptive master* a person may go wrong.[^1][^3] One says no interpretation is needed; the other says expert guidance is.

**A third, on the physiology.** The occipital and ear-nāḍī routes are asserted in anatomical vocabulary without anatomical support, as elsewhere in this build. `[LOW CONFIDENCE]` as a claim about the body.

**And the standing scope limit.** These are marks on the ladder footnote 518 calls false stages, and the instruction to ignore them is consistent with that footnote in a way the rest of the apparatus is not.[^5]

**Open questions.** Does visionary content actually track the practitioner's tradition as tightly as the claim requires — and are there documented cases of practitioners receiving figures from traditions they did not hold? And if both Chan and Christian contemplation developed standing warnings, what does the comparative base rate look like?

## Author Tensions & Convergences

Against [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/psychic-abilities-as-occipital-chi-pressure|Psychic Abilities as Occipital Chi Pressure]], these two pages split one mechanism between knowing and perceiving, and were built to be read as a pair. That page takes the accuracy profile of psi impressions; this one takes the phenomenology and the content-supply problem. **The same site produces both**, which is either the mechanism's strength or its indiscriminacy depending on how much you want from it.

The convergence with [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/du-yin-and-the-psi-programmes|Du-Yin and the Psi Programmes]] is exact and supplies what this page's physiology cannot. The occipital route explains why an event occurs; the du-yin explains what fills it — an image-faculty running on stored material without sensory correction. **Chi opens the door and the du-yin walks through it**, and the two chapters never state that jointly.

Read with [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/this-is-not-sainthood|This Is Not Sainthood]], the treatments are complementary and differently weighted. The *Śūraṅgama* grants each vision at full strength and forbids the conclusion; this page explains where the vision came from. **Scripture handles the interpretation and physiology handles the aetiology**, and the practical instruction that falls out of both is the same one.

Against [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/dry-wisdom-and-dead-tree-zen|Dry Wisdom and Dead Tree Zen]], there is a real strain. That page says suppressing the arising phenomena stalls the transformation and the correction is to let them proliferate. This one says ignore the visions entirely as māra. Ignoring and suppressing are not the same act — but the difference is not stated anywhere, and a practitioner told to ignore visions and not to suppress sensations has been given two instructions whose boundary is unmarked.

## Cross-Domain Handshakes

**A real event whose content the receiver supplies** — [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/idealization-as-transpersonal-projection|Idealization as Transpersonal Projection]]. That page's argument is that most psychoanalytic schools treat idealization as merely a defence to be analysed away, and that this misses something: the idealizing patient is projecting genuinely transpersonal material onto a human figure, so the *content* is not simply invention even though its *object* is wrong. The visionary case has exactly that structure. Something is occurring — the physiology is doing something real, and both Nan and Keating grant that the experience is not manufactured — and the figure it arrives wearing is supplied by the recipient's own store. **What the pairing gives that neither side gives alone: the identity of the figure and the reality of the event are independent variables, and confusing them is what both traditions' warning literature exists to prevent.** A practitioner who concludes the vision was invented because Christ appeared to a Christian has made the same error, in the opposite direction, as one who concludes Christ was there — both are reading the figure as evidence about the event. And it explains why the correction has to be procedural rather than interpretive in both fields: you cannot analyse your way to the right attribution from inside the experience, so the analyst brackets the object and works with what the material shows about the patient, while the Zen instruction brackets everything and says pass through.

*One handshake.* A second — the interpretive container fixing what an experience means — is carried in this hub by the *Śūraṅgama* refrain page and would be restatement.

## The Live Edge

**Sharpest implication.** **The mechanism is the same in every head and the visitor is always local — which means the identity of whoever appears is the one part of a visionary experience that carries no information about anything except the person having it.**

**Generative questions.**
- Does visionary content track the practitioner's tradition as tightly as the claim needs — and are there documented cases of figures from traditions the visionary did not hold?
- Both Chan and Christian contemplation developed standing warnings about this. What does that say about the comparative base rate, and has anyone compared them?
- Ignore the visions; do not suppress the sensations. Where is the line, and can a practitioner find it from inside?

## Connected Concepts

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/psychic-abilities-as-occipital-chi-pressure|Psychic Abilities as Occipital Chi Pressure]] — the same site, taken for knowing rather than perceiving
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/du-yin-and-the-psi-programmes|Du-Yin and the Psi Programmes]] — the faculty that fills the door the chi opens

# The Three Stages of Archetypal Embodiment

There is a question anyone doing devotional practice eventually runs into. You begin by loving someone else. If the practice works, the distance closes. **So what exactly are you doing at the end — still loving someone, or discovering you were never two?**[^1]

**Most traditions answer that question once and build everything on the answer.** ⚑ **One document in the Hanumanic Strategy corpus refuses to answer it and stages it instead** — **three years, three stances, one practitioner, moving from relationship to identity to neither.**[^1] ⚠ **And in the same document it places the one binding limit the corpus contains.**

## Four Technologies, and What Each Is Assigned

**The architecture is four × three: four practice-technologies, three stages, and every stage receives all four.**[^1]

- **Visualisation** — works on *"your mental body and imagination to create clear connection with Hanuman's qualities."*
- **Mantra** — works on the energetic body, *"sound vibration that literally restructures your consciousness at the vibrational level."*
- **Mudrā** — ⚑ **and this one is given a job the others cannot do**: it *"directs and concentrates the energy that mantra generates while creating physical anchor points for spiritual states."*
- **Ritual** — *"integrates all of these inner developments with your practical daily activities, ensuring that spiritual development serves your effectiveness in the world rather than becoming escapist fantasy."*

⚑⚑ **The division is not decorative and the mudrā clause is the tell.** ⚠ **Three of the four generate something; one of them *holds* what the others generate.** **That is a claim about failure modes — the document is saying that devotional practice loses its product between sessions, and that a physical anchor is what stops the leak.**

⚑ **Whether that is true is untested. That it is a specific mechanical claim, rather than a list of four nice things, is what makes the architecture worth recording.**

## Stage One — Relationship, and the Guard Against Becoming

**Year one. Fifteen minutes each morning, facing east.**[^1]

**Three minutes of settling. Then Hanumān visualised seated in front of you** — *"at a comfortable distance where you can clearly see his form while maintaining a natural sense of reverence"* — **in classical iconography, golden-bodied, hands in blessing.** **Five minutes holding the visualisation and letting *"whatever natural communication wants to arise"* arise.** **Close by offering the day's activities to the same divine consciousness Hanumān serves.**

**Mantra: *Om Hanumate Namaḥ*, twenty-one repetitions**, on a mālā if available, moved with thumb and middle finger — *"avoiding the use of your index finger, which represents ego consciousness."* **Then three repetitions before any significant task, difficult conversation, or moment of noticing anxiety or discouragement.**

**Mudrā: palms together at the heart, fingers interlocked, thumbs upward** — *"unified strength while maintaining the devotional attitude appropriate for Stage One."*

**Ritual: five minutes cleaning and ordering the workspace before touching any screen; thirty seconds dedicating creative work before beginning it; an evening review of moments acted from the archetype's qualities and moments acted from ego, fear or the wish for recognition.**

⭐ **The stance is stated explicitly and it is a prohibition**: *"maintaining healthy recognition that you are developing relationship with divine consciousness* ***rather than attempting to become divine consciousness through personal effort***. *This fundamental distinction prevents spiritual ego inflation."*

⚑⚑ **The corpus is elsewhere accused — including by itself — of collapsing devotion into identification too fast.**[^2] **Here it forbids the collapse for a year, and gives the reason.**

## Stage Two — When the Qualities Become Yours

**Year two, and the shift is doctrinal rather than technical.** *"The qualities Hanuman represents exist as potentials within your own deepest nature that devotional practice makes accessible."*[^1]

**The visualisation extends**: after five minutes of the established form, **golden light bridges his heart-centre to yours**, and his qualities are *"drawn into your own being through conscious visualisation and energetic reception rather than through mental effort."* **Strength arrives *"not as muscular power but as unshakeable inner stability."*** **And the devotional awakening is named as the stage's actual content** — *"your individual love for divine consciousness becomes strong enough to serve as your primary motivation for all activities."*

⚑ **The safeguard is that both terms stay in view**: *"you're not trying to disappear into Hanuman's energy or lose your individual personality, but rather to discover how your unique individual expression can serve as a vehicle."*

**Mantra escalates to three components**: *Om Hanumate Namaḥ* ×21 as preparation, then ***Om Rām Hanumate Tejase Namaḥ* ×108** — glossed in the document word by word, *"Rām"* the divine consciousness served, *"Hanumate"* the archetypal presence, *"Tejase"* *"to the radiant spiritual energy,"* *"Namaḥ"* the offering of one's own consciousness as its vehicle — **then *So-Ham* ×21**, *"which acknowledges your essential identity with universal consciousness while maintaining the proper humility."*

**Mudrā: right hand in *abhaya*, palm forward; left hand on the heart, palm inward.** ⚑ **The document explains the asymmetry**: right invokes archetypal power, left *"anchors that power in your individual heart centre rather than allowing it to create spiritual inflation or loss of practical grounding."*

## Stage Three — When Neither Term Survives

**Year three and beyond. Thirty minutes minimum.**[^1]

**The bridge is not built; the separation is allowed to dissolve** — *"not through mental effort but through complete devotional surrender that recognizes your individual consciousness as already being an expression of the same universal consciousness that manifests as all archetypal forms."*

⭐ **And the stance is stated with unusual precision**: *"you are neither the individual person seeking spiritual development nor the archetypal consciousness manifesting through individual form, but rather* ***the universal awareness within which both individual and archetypal consciousness appear*** *as temporary expressions."*

**Mantra becomes three fifty-four-fold sequences**: ***Om Namaḥ Śivāya*** *"to acknowledge universal consciousness as the source of all archetypal manifestations including Hanuman's specific qualities"* · ***Rām Rām Rām*** · ***Om Tat Sat***, *"which ensures that your archetypal embodiment remains grounded in authentic spiritual realization rather than becoming subtle spiritual materialism."*

**Mudrā: *cin-mudrā* in both hands, remaining fingers interlaced at the heart** — identity with universal consciousness in the thumb-and-index join, **the devotional heart and service capacity in the interlacing.**

**Ritual: *"sahaja bhāva"* — *"the complete dissolution of the sense of individual spiritual practitioner while maintaining perfect effectiveness in all practical responsibilities."***

## The Mudrās Track the Stances Exactly

⚑⚑ **Read the three hand positions in sequence and they are an argument, not an ornament.**

**Stage One: two palms pressed together, thumbs up.** ⚑ **A closed circuit, entirely within the practitioner, oriented upward. One party, addressing another.**

**Stage Two: one hand out, one hand in.** ⚑ **The circuit is open on one side. Power enters, and is held somewhere it cannot inflate.** **Two terms, joined and distinguished.**

**Stage Three: both hands making the same sign, joined at the heart.** ⚑ **Symmetry restored, but at a different level — the gesture that in Indian iconography marks teaching and pure awareness, doubled and brought to the seat of devotion.**

⭐ **Whatever one makes of the metaphysics, the notation is coherent**, and it is the kind of coherence that is hard to produce accidentally. ⚠ **The document never remarks on it.**

## The Gates Are Behavioural, and They Are Set Outside the Practice

⭐⭐ **The progression criteria are the best thing in the document and they answer a defect the build recorded three phases ago.**

**Stage One is complete when devotional connection *"feels natural and reliable rather than requiring conscious effort to maintain,"* and when the archetypal qualities are available *"during challenging practical circumstances rather than only during formal spiritual practice periods."***[^1]

**Stage Two is complete when *"your individual activities naturally express dharmic principles rather than requiring conscious effort to maintain spiritual perspective* ***during business responsibilities and personal relationships***.*"*

⚑⚑ **Both are first-person, both are checkable, and both are set in ordinary life rather than on the cushion.** ⚠ **Compare the corpus's other progression apparatus, in which the markers are overwhelmingly other people's reports** — *"colleagues notice increased emotional stability," "others naturally drawn to seek guidance"*[^3] — **which the practitioner cannot audit and the reader cannot check.**

⭐ **So the corpus has two kinds of gate and does not distinguish them.** ⚑ **This document's kind asks whether the thing has become effortless where it is hardest.** **The other kind asks whether people have noticed.** ⚠ **And a further year is added to every stage by a plain rule: *"each stage requires approximately one full year of consistent daily practice before attempting progression."***

## The One Gate That Binds

⭐⭐⭐ **And here the document does something nothing else in the read corpus does. It makes a limit a condition of entry, and it states it three times.**[^1]

> *"The practices for Stage Three require complete dedication and* ***the guidance of authentic spiritual community***.*"*

> *"This practice should only be undertaken after mastering Stage Two development and preferably* ***with guidance from authentic spiritual teachers who have completed similar development themselves***.*"*

> *"Stage Three practices should only be undertaken when Stage Two identification has become completely natural and stable,* ***and when you have access to authentic spiritual community that can provide guidance and validation***.*"*

**And the reason is given**: *"regular engagement with your existing spiritual community… provides* ***external validation*** *that your development remains authentic and beneficial rather than becoming* ***isolated personal process that could develop in problematic directions***.*"*

⚑⚑⚑ **The build has recorded for three phases that this corpus lacks the external check a tradition supplies.** ⚠ **That finding is now wrong as stated.** ⭐ **The check exists in six documents of this cluster, and here it is not advice but a precondition** — **alongside a referral boundary elsewhere in the same cluster that hands the practitioner to medicine, psychology or law when the difficulty is not spiritual.**[^4]

⚠ **What remains true is narrower and should replace the old claim: the limit is stated and not enforced.** ⚑ **No mechanism prevents a reader from beginning Stage Three alone, and the gate sits in a closing section headed *Integration Guidelines and Safety Considerations* — the last thing in the document.**[^5] ⚑⚑ **Which is the corpus's characteristic failure, not an absence of judgement: the judgement is there and it is shelved.**

⛔ **One architectural fact, recorded without its contents.** **The three stages are declared a superstructure on a received foundational practice which must be *maintained throughout and not replaced*** — *"maintain your foundational practices throughout all stages of Hanumanic development rather than replacing them with advanced techniques."* ⚑ **A system claiming three years of escalating attainment, telling the reader its own advanced work is not a substitute for what he was already doing. The relation is the finding; the received practice is not recorded here.**

## Implementation Workflow

**Do not begin at Stage Two because Stage One looks preliminary.** ⚑ **The document's own gate is that Stage One is not finished until the connection survives difficulty, and the prohibition on *becoming* is load-bearing for a year.**

**Use the behavioural criteria, not the calendar.** ⚑ **The year is a floor, not a measure.** **What actually gates is whether the thing has gone effortless in business and in relationships, which is checkable weekly.**

**Read the mudrā sequence as the argument.** ⚑ **If a stage's hand position does not match the stance you are actually in, the stance is what is wrong.**

**Secure the external party before Stage Three, not during it.** ⚠ **The document names this as a precondition and then does not enforce it. Enforce it yourself, or do not enter the stage.**

**And keep whatever foundation you already have.** ⚑ **The system says so itself, in the section a reader is most likely to skip.**

## Evidence, Tensions, Open Questions

**Source.** *The Hanumanic Transformation Manual: Sacred Practices for Each Stage*, read in full 2026-08-18 with the thirty-one other documents of the remaining folder clusters.[^1] `personal-notes`. `[EXTENSION]` — **the four-by-three architecture, the staged mantras and the mudrā sequence are the author's synthesis.**

⛔ **RECEIVED-PRACTICE RULING APPLIED.** **The foundational practice the manual names as its non-negotiable substrate is recorded here only as a structural relation.** **Its contents, instructions and lineage material appear nowhere on this page.**

⚠ **Bounded.** **The claim that this is the only *binding* external-party gate in the corpus is a claim about the sixty-one folder documents read as of 2026-08-18** — phases 1B, 3, 7, 8, 9 and 9a. **Forty-four remain unread and nothing is claimed about them.**

🔴 **Preserved.** **This document's progression gates are first-person and behavioural; a document in the same cluster gates progress on third-party report; a third document in that same sub-cluster insists assessment must be *"independent… without relying on external validation."***[^3] ⚑ **Three positions on one question, in one corpus, none citing another. Recorded, not reconciled.**

🔴 **Also preserved.** **The three-stage arc is one of twelve mutually incompatible progression schemes in this corpus, and one of six that are three-part.** ⚠ **None agrees with another on duration and none gives a reason for its durations.**[^5]

**Open question.** ⚑ **Is the three-stage sequence a curriculum or a doctrine?** **If the stages are pedagogical, the earlier stances are scaffolding to be discarded.** **If they are doctrinal, Stage One's prohibition on identification is either true or false, and Stage Two contradicts it.** ⚠ **The document does not say, and the difference decides whether a practitioner at Stage Three should regard Stage One as a mistake he has outgrown or a truth he still holds.**

## Author Tensions & Convergences

⚑ **The author who stages the identification question is the same author who elsewhere claims identification as his innovation.**

⚠ **The corpus's standing self-description is that its two central practices — identification and shadow-integration — are departures from a tradition that supposedly holds neither.**[^2] ⚑⚑ **This document quietly disproves half of that from the inside: it does not treat identification as a novelty to be defended but as a *middle term*, arrived at after a year of explicitly refusing it and superseded after another year.** ⭐ **A writer who thought identification was his invention would not build a stage above it.**

⚑ **Which suggests the corpus's novelty claims are not beliefs so much as framing habits** — **and the build has recorded the cost of that framing precisely: a practitioner who believes he is trespassing cannot go looking for the tradition's limits, because on his own account there are none.**[^2] ⚠ **Here the limits were found anyway, because the practice architecture demanded them.**

## Cross-Domain Handshakes

**[[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/the-three-darshanas-simultaneously-true-hanuman|The Three Darśanas, Simultaneously True of Hanuman]].** ⚑⚑ **The exact structural counterpart, and the pairing is the strongest this phase produced.** That page holds the Aṅka's position that **three incompatible philosophical readings of Hanumān — duality, qualified non-duality, non-duality — are all true of him at once**, held simultaneously by a volume constituted to hold disagreement. ⭐ **This document arranges the same three positions* ***sequentially***, as one practitioner's three years: Stage One is a relation between two; Stage Two is identity-in-participation, named in the document as *"non-dual devotion"*; Stage Three is neither term surviving. ⚑⚑⚑ **The insight neither page reaches alone: the difference between holding the three at once and walking through them in order is the difference between a claim about a deity and a curriculum for a person.** ⚠ **A theology can afford simultaneity because nothing has to be done on Tuesday. A practice cannot, because a practitioner has to know which stance to take up this morning** — **so the sequence is not a weaker version of the simultaneity, it is what the simultaneity becomes when someone has to live it.** ⭐ **And that reframes the corpus's whole relation to the volume: this is not a modern simplification of a subtle traditional position, it is the operational form the subtle position was always going to require.** **Neither document knows the other exists.**

## The Live Edge

⚑ **The manual assumes the three stances are *stages* — that Stage Two supersedes Stage One and Stage Three supersedes both.**

⚠ **The Aṅka's position is that all three are true at once. If that is right, the manual is not describing development but* ***attention***: three things always the case, foregrounded one at a time.** ⚑⚑ **And those two readings have opposite consequences for a practitioner in difficulty.** **On the developmental reading, someone at Stage Three who finds himself simply loving Hanumān has regressed.** **On the simultaneity reading, he has done nothing of the kind — he has picked up a stance that never stopped being available.**

🧭 **The open question the corpus walks up to and does not answer: is there a stance a practitioner can lose?** ⚑ **Every progression scheme in this corpus assumes there is — that attainment is cumulative and one-directional.** ⚠ **Nothing in either corpus tests it, and the tradition's own most careful statement on Hanumān points the other way.**

🧭 **The sharper version, and it is the chapter: if the three darśanas are simultaneously true, then the year-per-stage rule is not a safety measure but a category error** — **and the manual's genuinely good behavioural gates would be measuring fluency in a stance rather than progress toward a state.** ⭐ **Which is a better thing to measure, and the document is one sentence away from saying so.**

## Connected Concepts

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/the-three-darshanas-simultaneously-true-hanuman|The Three Darśanas, Simultaneously True of Hanuman]] — the same three positions, held at once rather than in sequence
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/the-recognition-signs-are-other-peoples-reports|The Recognition Signs Are Other People's Reports]] — the progression apparatus this document's gates repair
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/faith-in-the-lord-itself-is-hanuman|Faith in the Lord Itself Is Hanuman]] — the volume's own most compressed statement of the identity question
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/the-deity-as-a-variable|The Deity as a Variable]] — how far the technology separates from its object
- [[ARCHIVES/sources/hanumanic-strategy-corpus|The Hanumanic Strategy Corpus]] — the extension corpus and its limitations
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/hubs/hanumanic-strategy-hub|Hanumanic Strategy Hub]] — the build this page belongs to

## Footnotes

[^1]: [[ARCHIVES/sources/hanumanic-strategy-corpus|The Hanumanic Strategy Corpus]] — `personal-notes`, authored extension. *The Hanumanic Transformation Manual: Sacred Practices for Each Stage*, read in full 2026-08-18. Source of: the four sacred technologies with their assigned bodies and the mudrā's stated holding function; **Stage One** (fifteen minutes facing east, the seated visualisation at *"a comfortable distance,"* *Om Hanumate Namaḥ* ×21 with the index-finger prohibition, the interlocked-fingers mudrā, the three daily rituals, and the prohibition *"you are developing relationship with divine consciousness rather than attempting to become divine consciousness through personal effort"*); **Stage Two** (the heart-to-heart bridge of light, *"the qualities Hanuman represents exist as potentials within your own deepest nature,"* *"non-dual devotion,"* *Om Rām Hanumate Tejase Namaḥ* ×108 with its word-by-word gloss, *So-Ham* ×21, the abhaya-plus-heart mudrā and its stated asymmetry); **Stage Three** (thirty minutes, the dissolution *"not through mental effort but through complete devotional surrender,"* the *"neither the individual person… nor the archetypal consciousness"* formulation, *Om Namaḥ Śivāya* / *Rām Rām Rām* / *Om Tat Sat* at ×54 each, *cin-mudrā* with añjali, *"sahaja bhāva"*); **the behavioural progression criteria for Stages One and Two**; **the one-year-per-stage rule**; **all three statements of the Stage Three community requirement and the *"external validation… isolated personal process that could develop in problematic directions"* rationale**; and **the instruction to maintain the received foundational practice throughout rather than replacing it.** `[EXTENSION]`

[^2]: [[ARCHIVES/sources/hanumanic-strategy-corpus|The Hanumanic Strategy Corpus]] — `personal-notes`. Phase 1B's governing finding, recorded in this build's governing document: the corpus frames both identification and shadow-integration as departures from a tradition that in fact holds both positions, and the cost of the mistake is safety rather than embarrassment — a practitioner who believes he is trespassing cannot look for the tradition's limits, because on his own account there are none.

[^3]: [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/the-recognition-signs-are-other-peoples-reports|The Recognition Signs Are Other People's Reports]] — this build's page, for the corpus's progression-gating apparatus built on third-party attribution the practitioner cannot audit; and, added at phase 9a, for the third position in the same sub-cluster insisting that competency indicators be assessable *"independently without relying on external validation."*

[^4]: [[ARCHIVES/sources/hanumanic-strategy-corpus|The Hanumanic Strategy Corpus]] — `personal-notes`. *The Hanumanic Cultivation Operating System: Crisis-to-Mastery Integration Technology*, read in full 2026-08-18; its `Critical Safety Parameters` name *"regular assessment with trusted spiritual community to catch ego inflation early,"* *"never using spiritual authority to avoid necessary professional skill development,"* and *"recognizing when challenges require professional support (medical, psychological, legal) rather than spiritual approaches alone."*

[^5]: [[ARCHIVES/sources/hanumanic-strategy-corpus|The Hanumanic Strategy Corpus]] — `personal-notes`. the-twelve-jyotirlingas.content:

domain: eastern-spirituality
